messages:
Alex M: Quick sync—who owns the mapping between tenant SLO thresholds and notify routing policies in the console? We need a DRI to unblock the tenant-override UI work.
Priya K: I thought this was split—console owns the UI + persist layer, notify-service owns runtime routing. But there's a gray area for default->tenant override merging.
Tom R: Correct. Console saves an AlertPolicy proto, notify-service translates that into routing decisions. The problem: console currently lets users edit `notify_tier` but doesn't validate compatibility with tenant contracts.
Sasha L: We keep getting incidents where customers set low thresholds and never receive alerts because routing falls back to global suppression. Need a clear ownership for merge behavior and a contract.
Erin (oncall): +1. Last week's support case: customer set threshold=2% error_budget, expected pagers, but notify routed to low-priority queue. We need either console validation or an explicit flag `force_escalation`.
Alex M: Proposal: console writes AlertPolicy plus an optional `routingHint` object. notify-service treats `routingHint.priority` as advisory unless `force_escalation=true`. That keeps backwards compatibility.
Priya K: Sounds OK. API sketch:
```json
{
  "policy_id": "p-123",
  "threshold_pct": 2,
  "notify_tier": "critical",
  "routing_hint": { "priority": "pager", "force_escalation": false }
}
```
Tom R: If we add that field, notify-service needs to expose rejection reasons for invalid combos (e.g., tenant has quiet_window). Console should show those validation errors inline before save.
Sasha L: Also need UX for tenant overrides vs inherited defaults. Suggest a small banner: "This setting differs from account default. Click to view merge result." Minimal, not a modal.
Erin (oncall): Operational ask: when notify-service downgrades due to suppression rules, it should emit a telemetry event with `policy_id` and `reason` so console can surface an explanation in the alert details. That will reduce paging confusion.
Tom R: Agree. We can add event `notify.routing.decision` with tags {policy_id, decision: "downgrade|escalate|route_default", reason}.
Priya K: One more: rollout plan. We should feature-flag validation and routingHint UI. Rollout steps: 1) add telemetry + no-op in notify-service, 2) console UI + send routingHint (flag off), 3) enable validation (flag on), 4) flip default `force_escalation` behavior if we decide to.
Alex M: Timeline? We want to ship tenant-override UI in 3 sprints, but need the DRI and API contract this week.
Sasha L: I'll DRI the UI. @Tom R can you own the API contract and telemetry?
Tom R: I can. I'll PR a draft proto and a small event schema today.
DeployBot: New PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/notify-service/pulls/987 (proto + telemetry).
Erin (oncall): Thanks. Also request: include an `audit.reason` field when console auto-merges a tenant override so oncall can trace back.
Priya K: Good call. Add `audit: { source: "console", merged_from: "default" }`.
Alex M: Great. Next actions: Sasha to start UI mockups, Tom to post proto, Priya to draft console validation UX copy. We'll sync Friday. :thumbsup:
Sasha L: Noted. I'll post mocks in #design once ready.
Tom R: Linking proto PR in this thread when ready.
Erin (oncall): If anyone touches paging logic, ping oncall before flipping defaults. We can't risk increased pages during the rollout.
Alex M: Agreed. End of thread."
